findings.where: First screen at desktop and phone, and the whole page: the hero, the nav (Profile, Articles, Blog) and the foot of the sheet
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The email address isn't shown, there is no contact link or button, and the nav has no Contact item. The parts map lists only three nav links, a download link and a replay button. The palette and texture notes both describe a pad-yellow address strip at the foot of the sheet, but it never appears on the page.
findings.who_objects: The bank official who has read the line and decided Mark could be their PPP-law advisor now has nothing to click and no address to copy. They would have to search for him elsewhere. The founder would object too: the brief's first test asks for one direct, personal way to reach Mark, with the address shown, on the first screen.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel near the foot of the page (desktop-05, phone-03/04)
findings.fault: The panel sits on a saturated lavender block. That colour is in neither the palette nor the house colours. In the overview it is the loudest mass on the page and pulls the eye before the article does. It also breaks the direction's own premise of one soft paper ground with grey and blue as the only ink.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for the house blue and grey and one quiet ground. The visitor would object too: a lilac slab at the end of a sober legal document reads as playful and out of place for a counsel's-paper identity.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and the 'Download' heading
findings.fault: Both subheads are set in a heavy, wide grotesque. This is a third typeface that the type pair doesn't include, since the pair says Newsreader 500 for subheads. Against the light, refined serif text it reads blunt and slightly techy, and it breaks the article's voice at exactly the points Angélique will add most often.
findings.who_objects: The visitor reading Mark's argument, who meets a jarring, poster-like change of tone mid-article. The founder would object too, having asked for serious, refined type and nothing in-your-face techy.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lectern photograph's frame
findings.fault: The photo's backdrop is printed as a solid dark-grey slab the full width of the column. That makes it the heaviest block in the article, against the palette note that photographs are multiplied onto the paper and take its warmth. The image reads as a dark box dropped onto the page, not a photograph printed on it.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning the article, whose eye is dragged to a heavy dark rectangle rather than the text. Mark too, whose 'journal' look is lost to a slab of grey.

findings.where: First screen: the name block, the line and the supporting paragraph
findings.fault: Nothing on the first screen says where Mark works or which regions he has advised in. His one credential, 'Formerly Lead Lawyer, PPP Group, World Bank', is also the only proof of work. There is no newest talk or article with its venue and date to show he is active now.
findings.who_objects: The bank official screening advisors against terms of reference. They judge relevant experience by region and recent assignments, and here they can't tell whether he has worked in their region or recently.

findings.fault: The swatches come in four unrelated shapes: a square-cornered box, a rounded box, an ellipse, and a box with a thick blue border. The difference means nothing. And since blue is the palette's focus and link colour, the blue-bordered yellow swatch looks selected or focused.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the tile as the identity's rules. Arbitrary shape changes suggest a looser system than the direction claims, and the blue edge hints at a state that doesn't exist.
